transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… I came in because I just feel real restless, like there’s a motor running inside me most of the day. I don’t mean to make it sound dramatic, but if I’ve got to sit still—like at church, or here at the clinic, or even at home—I start feeling trapped, like I’ve got to get up or do something. I’m not sure if that’s the right way to explain it.
Have you started or changed any medications—especially antipsychotics or other psychiatric drugs—in the weeks before this restlessness began?

Um… I don’t think so, no. I mean, I haven’t started anything like that that I can think of. I’m not real familiar with all the names, but I don’t believe there was any new psychiatric medicine or anything changed right before this. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you been using any stimulants, recreational drugs, or unusually large amounts of caffeine recently?
I don’t think so, Doctor. I mean… I drink coffee sometimes, but I wouldn’t say it’s anything crazy, unless I’m not thinking of it right. No drugs or anything like that. Is that what you mean?

When you feel this restlessness, do you also notice yourself worrying a lot about different things—like your health, work, or family—or is it mainly just a physical urge to move without any particular worried thoughts attached?

It’s more like the body part, I think. I mean, I worry some like anybody, but when this happens it’s not really me sitting there thinking about work or family or my health. It’s just… I feel like there’s a motor going inside me, and if I’m sitting at church or here or even at home, I start feeling kind of trapped, like I need to get up and move. Is that making sense?
Thinking back, did you notice this kind of restless, 'motor running' feeling when you were a child or teenager, or is this something that started fairly recently in your life?

I guess… yeah, it goes back pretty far. I don’t want to make it sound like I was a bad kid or anything, but in school they were always moving my seat because I couldn’t really stay put. I’d talk when I wasn’t supposed to, and sometimes I’d jump up before class was even done and get in trouble for it. So… I think it’s been there since I was a boy, if that’s what you’re asking.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports a lifelong (since childhood) pattern of motor restlessness ('a motor running inside me'), inability to remain seated, fidgeting, talking out of turn, and impulsive movements (jumping up before class ended) that led to repeated correction in school. Current symptoms mirror this childhood pattern (restlessness in church, clinic, home) rather than being of recent onset. No temporal association with new psychiatric medications, stimulant use, or excessive caffeine intake, ruling out medication-induced akathisia (G25.71). The restlessness is described as purely physical/motor without accompanying anxious cognitive worry, arguing against Generalized Anxiety Disorder (F41.1). The chronicity from childhood, hyperactive-impulsive symptom cluster, and absence of an alternative medical or pharmacologic cause support a diagnosis of ADHD, predominantly hyperactive-impulsive presentation (F90.0).
